options: A network of wires that moves electricity to many places
A single battery that stores energy
grid.hint: The answer is "A network of wires that moves electricity to many places". A grid is a network of wires that carries electricity to many places.

grid.q: Which statement about the electrical grid is true?
options: It carries electricity from power plants to many places
It only works inside one flashlight
It carries water from lakes to homes
grid.hint: The answer is "It carries electricity from power plants to many places". The grid moves electricity from power plants to homes, schools, and stores.

grid.q: Fill in the blank: An electrical grid is a network of ___ that moves electricity.
grid.hint: The answer is "wires". Wires carry the electricity in a grid.

grid.q: Which term means a network of wires that transfers electricity from power plants to many places?
grid.hint: The answer is "Electrical grid". That is the meaning of electrical grid.

grid.q: In an electrical grid, where does the electricity start out?
options: At the light switch in your room
At energy sources like power plants
grid.hint: The answer is "At energy sources like power plants". The grid carries electricity from energy sources and power plants out to many places.

grid.q: Which of these is part of the electrical grid?
grid.hint: The answer is "Power lines along the street". Power lines are the wires that carry electricity in the grid.

grid.q: Which of these is NOT part of the electrical grid?
grid.hint: The answer is "A rubber band". A rubber band does not carry or make electricity for the grid.

grid.q: Which place gets electricity from the grid?
grid.hint: The answer is "A school building". The grid sends electricity to buildings like schools.

grid.q: Which group lists things that work together in a grid?
grid.hint: The answer is "Power plant, wires, homes". A grid uses wires to carry electricity from power plants to homes.

grid.q: Which is an example of the grid at work?
options: A battery running a toy car
Wires carrying electricity from a power plant to a town
grid.hint: The answer is "Wires carrying electricity from a power plant to a town". The grid moves electricity through wires from power plants to towns.

grid.q: Maya turns on a lamp plugged into the wall. How did the electricity get to her house?
options: From the lamp's light bulb itself
Through the wires of the electrical grid
grid.hint: The answer is "Through the wires of the electrical grid". Electricity travels from the power plant to her house through grid wires.

grid.q: A storm knocks down the power lines on your street. What most likely happens?
options: Homes on the street lose electricity
grid.hint: The answer is "Homes on the street lose electricity". If grid wires break, electricity cannot reach those homes.

grid.q: New houses are built far from town. What must workers add so the houses get electricity from the power plant?
options: Wires that connect to the grid
grid.hint: The answer is "Wires that connect to the grid". Houses need grid wires to receive electricity from the power plant.

grid.q: In a class model, Sam uses yarn to connect a toy power plant to many toy houses. What does the yarn stand for?
options: The fuel for the power plant
grid.hint: The answer is "The wires of the grid". In a grid, wires connect power plants to many places.

grid.q: Why does a city need a big grid of wires?
options: To move electricity to many different places
grid.hint: The answer is "To move electricity to many different places". A grid transfers electricity from power plants to many places.

options: One part that works all alone
Connected parts that work together to give electricity to devices
elsystem.hint: The answer is "Connected parts that work together to give electricity to devices". An electrical system is a group of connected parts working together to provide electricity.

elsystem.q: Which statement about an electrical system is true?
options: Its parts are connected and work together
elsystem.hint: The answer is "Its parts are connected and work together". An electrical system is a group of connected parts that work together.

elsystem.q: Fill in the blank: An electrical system is a group of connected parts that work ___ to provide electricity to devices.
elsystem.hint: The answer is "together". The parts of an electrical system work together.

elsystem.q: Which term means a group of connected parts that work together to provide electricity to devices?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "Electrical system". That is the meaning of electrical system.

elsystem.q: What is the job of an electrical system?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "To provide electricity to devices". An electrical system provides electricity to devices.

elsystem.q: Which is an example of an electrical system?
options: A flashlight with batteries, wires, and a bulb
elsystem.hint: The answer is "A flashlight with batteries, wires, and a bulb". A flashlight's connected parts work together to give the bulb electricity.

elsystem.q: Which is a part of a house's electrical system?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "Wires inside the walls". Wires in the walls connect parts that bring electricity to devices.

elsystem.q: Which group of parts could make a simple electrical system?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "Battery, wires, and a bulb". A battery, wires, and a bulb can connect and work together.

elsystem.q: Which is NOT part of a car's electrical system?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "The rubber tires". Tires help the car roll but do not provide electricity.

elsystem.q: Battery, switch, wire... which item belongs in this group?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "Light bulb". A light bulb is a part that connects into an electrical system.

elsystem.q: Leo builds a circuit for the science fair, but one wire is not connected. What happens?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "The bulb does not light". All the parts must be connected for the system to work.

elsystem.q: Why does a doorbell need its button, wires, and bell all connected?
options: The parts work together to get electricity to the bell
elsystem.hint: The answer is "The parts work together to get electricity to the bell". In an electrical system, connected parts work together.

elsystem.q: Mia's toy car has a battery, wires, and a motor all connected. What is this group of parts called?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "An electrical system". Connected parts that provide electricity to a device make an electrical system.

elsystem.q: In class, Ms. Lee takes the battery out of a working circuit. What happens to the bulb?
elsystem.hint: The answer is "It goes out". Without one of its parts, the system cannot give the bulb electricity.

elsystem.q: A video game console's power cord gets cut. Why does it stop working?
options: A part of its electrical system is broken
elsystem.hint: The answer is "A part of its electrical system is broken". The cord is a part of the system, so the system cannot do its job.

options: A time when electricity stops working in an area
A time when the sun goes down
A time when there is extra electricity
blackout.hint: The answer is "A time when electricity stops working in an area". A blackout is when electricity stops working in an area.

blackout.q: Which statement about blackouts is true?
options: Blackouts can happen only in the daytime
During a blackout, an area loses electricity
During a blackout, lights get brighter
blackout.hint: The answer is "During a blackout, an area loses electricity". In a blackout, electricity stops working in an area.

blackout.q: Fill in the blank: A blackout is a time when ___ stops working in an area.
blackout.hint: The answer is "electricity". A blackout is about electricity stopping.

blackout.q: Which term means a time when electricity stops working in an area?
blackout.hint: The answer is "Blackout". That is the meaning of blackout.

blackout.q: A blackout affects how much space?
options: A whole area, like a street or town
Only one toy with a dead battery
blackout.hint: The answer is "A whole area, like a street or town". A blackout is electricity stopping in an area.

blackout.q: Which is an example of a blackout?
options: All the lights on your street go out after a storm
You turn off your bedroom lamp
blackout.hint: The answer is "All the lights on your street go out after a storm". A blackout is when electricity stops working in a whole area.

options: Every house on your block loses power
You switch off the TV to go to bed
blackout.hint: The answer is "You switch off the TV to go to bed". Turning off one TV is your choice; a blackout is electricity stopping in an area.

blackout.q: Which would still work during a blackout?
blackout.hint: The answer is "A flashlight with batteries". Batteries store their own energy, so they do not need the wall power.

blackout.q: Which would stop working during a blackout?
options: A refrigerator plugged into the wall
blackout.hint: The answer is "A refrigerator plugged into the wall". Things plugged into the wall need electricity from the grid.

blackout.q: Which list has only things that still work in a blackout?
blackout.hint: The answer is "Battery flashlight, candle, battery radio". These do not need wall electricity to work.

blackout.q: During a storm, every light in your neighborhood goes dark at once. What is happening?
blackout.hint: The answer is "A blackout". Electricity stopped working in the whole area.

blackout.q: During a long blackout, why does the ice cream in the freezer start to melt?
options: The ice cream turns into wind
The freezer gets too much electricity
blackout.hint: The answer is "The freezer has no electricity". Without electricity, the freezer cannot keep food cold.

blackout.q: During a blackout at school, why can't the class watch a video on the smartboard?
options: The smartboard is made of wood
blackout.hint: The answer is "The smartboard needs electricity". In a blackout there is no electricity for the smartboard.

blackout.q: Grandpa keeps a battery radio for blackouts. Why?
options: It makes electricity for the whole town
Its batteries give energy when the wall power is out
blackout.hint: The answer is "Its batteries give energy when the wall power is out". Batteries are an energy source that works without the grid.

blackout.q: A tree falls on the power lines that bring electricity to your town. What do you predict?
options: The town may have a blackout
blackout.hint: The answer is "The town may have a blackout". If electricity cannot reach the town, it stops working there.

options: When a system gets new parts
When a system cannot do its job properly
failure.hint: The answer is "When a system cannot do its job properly". A system failure is when a system cannot perform its function properly.

failure.q: Which statement about a system failure is true?
options: The system cannot do its job well
It only happens to the sun
failure.hint: The answer is "The system cannot do its job well". In a system failure, the system cannot perform its job properly.

failure.q: Fill in the blank: A system failure is when a system cannot perform its ___ properly.
failure.hint: The answer is "function". Function means the system's job.

failure.q: Which term means when a system cannot perform its job properly?
failure.hint: The answer is "System failure". That is the meaning of system failure.

failure.q: In the meaning of system failure, the word function means what?
failure.hint: The answer is "Job". A system's function is its job.

failure.q: Which is an example of a system failure?
options: A fridge stops keeping food cold
A fridge keeps the milk cold
A lamp lights up when switched on
failure.hint: The answer is "A fridge stops keeping food cold". The fridge cannot do its job, so it is a system failure.

failure.q: Which is NOT a system failure?
options: A computer will not turn on
failure.hint: The answer is "A doorbell rings when pressed". The doorbell is doing its job properly.

options: A fan that spins when switched on
A heater that blows only cold air
failure.hint: The answer is "A heater that blows only cold air". A heater's job is to warm the air, so it is failing.

failure.q: Which list shows only system failures?
options: Loud radio, cold fridge, spinning fan
Dead phone screen, broken fan, dark streetlight
Bright lamp, warm oven, ringing bell
failure.hint: The answer is "Dead phone screen, broken fan, dark streetlight". Each of these cannot do its job properly.

failure.q: Which is a system failure in the electrical grid?
options: Power lines break and homes lose electricity
A power plant sends electricity to homes
failure.hint: The answer is "Power lines break and homes lose electricity". The grid cannot do its job of moving electricity.

failure.q: The class fish tank pump stops moving water, but everything else in the room still works. What is this?
failure.hint: The answer is "A system failure". Only the pump cannot do its job, so it is a system failure, not an area blackout.

failure.q: Zoe's science fair robot is supposed to roll forward, but it just sits still. What happened?
failure.hint: The answer is "Its system had a failure". The robot cannot do its job properly.

failure.q: Why is a blackout a kind of system failure?
options: The grid cannot do its job of moving electricity
The grid makes too much light
failure.hint: The answer is "The grid cannot do its job of moving electricity". A system failure is when a system cannot perform its function.

failure.q: The school heater fails on a freezing day. What do you predict?
failure.hint: The answer is "The classrooms get colder". The heater cannot do its job of warming the rooms.

failure.q: Your bike chain breaks, and pedaling no longer turns the wheels. Is this a system failure?
options: No, because bikes have no parts
No, the bike works better now
Yes, the bike cannot do its job
failure.hint: The answer is "Yes, the bike cannot do its job". The bike system cannot perform its function properly.

options: The place where something ends forever
The place where something comes from
source.hint: The answer is "The place where something comes from". A source is the place where something comes from.

options: A river's source is where its water comes from
A source is the end of something
A source is always a battery
source.hint: The answer is "A river's source is where its water comes from". A source is where something comes from.

source.q: Fill in the blank: A source is the ___ where something comes from.
source.hint: The answer is "place". A source is a place.

source.q: Which term means the place where something comes from?
source.hint: The answer is "Source". That is the meaning of source.

source.q: Asking for the source of something answers which question?
source.hint: The answer is "Where does it come from?". A source is the place where something comes from.

source.q: What is the source of milk?
source.hint: The answer is "A cow". Milk comes from cows.

source.q: What is the source of apples?
source.hint: The answer is "An apple tree". Apples come from apple trees.

source.q: What is the source of honey?
source.hint: The answer is "Bees". Honey comes from bees.

source.q: Which is NOT a source of wood?
source.hint: The answer is "A rock". Wood comes from trees, not rocks.

source.q: Which pair matches a thing with its source?
source.hint: The answer is "Eggs - chicken". Eggs come from chickens.

source.q: Ava follows a stream uphill to find where its water begins. What is she looking for?
source.hint: The answer is "The stream's source". The source is the place where the water comes from.

source.q: Your teacher asks where the paper in your notebook first came from. What is the best answer?
source.hint: The answer is "Trees". Paper is made from wood, which comes from trees.

source.q: For a class report, Jay lists the book where he found his facts. What is that book?
source.hint: The answer is "A source of information". The book is the place his facts came from.

source.q: You hear a crash in the kitchen and see a pot falling to the floor. What is the pot?
source.hint: The answer is "The source of the sound". The pot is where the sound came from.

source.q: Your wool sweater keeps you warm. What is the source of the wool?
source.hint: The answer is "Sheep". Wool comes from sheep.

esource.hint: The answer is "Something that provides energy". An energy source is something that provides energy.

options: The sun gives off no energy
Food is an energy source for your body
esource.hint: The answer is "Food is an energy source for your body". Food, the sun, and batteries all provide energy.

esource.q: Fill in the blank: An energy source is something that ___ energy.
esource.hint: The answer is "provides". Energy sources provide energy.

esource.q: Which term means something that provides energy?
esource.hint: The answer is "Energy source". That is the meaning of energy source.

esource.q: Which list names only energy sources?
esource.hint: The answer is "Sun, wind, water, food". Sun, wind, water, and food all provide energy.
The answer is "The sun". The sun provides light and heat energy.

esource.q: Which is NOT an energy source?
esource.hint: The answer is "An empty glass jar". An empty jar does not provide energy.

esource.q: What pushes a sailboat across the lake?
esource.hint: The answer is "Wind". Wind is an energy source that pushes the sail.

esource.q: Which energy source gives your body energy to run at recess?
esource.hint: The answer is "Food". Food provides energy for your body.

esource.q: Which energy source is inside a TV remote?
esource.hint: The answer is "Batteries". Batteries provide the energy for a remote.

esource.q: A family puts solar panels on their roof. Which energy source will the panels use?
esource.hint: The answer is "The sun". Solar panels use energy from the sun.

esource.q: Before a soccer game, Kai eats a banana. Why does that help him play?
options: Food is an energy source for his body
esource.hint: The answer is "Food is an energy source for his body". Food provides energy for the body.

esource.q: Mom's car stops because it ran out of gas. What does the car need?
esource.hint: The answer is "More fuel". Fuel like gas is an energy source for cars.

esource.q: A town builds a dam with big wheels that spin in a river. Which energy source is it using?
esource.hint: The answer is "Moving water". Moving water is an energy source.

esource.q: A science fair pinwheel spins only when a fan blows on it. What gives the pinwheel its energy?
esource.hint: The answer is "Moving air from the fan". Moving air, like wind, provides the energy that spins it.

options: Keeping energy in one form forever
Changing energy from one form into another
conversion.hint: The answer is "Changing energy from one form into another". Energy conversion is changing energy from one form into another.

options: Energy can change from one form into another
conversion.hint: The answer is "Energy can change from one form into another". Energy is never destroyed; it can be converted into other forms.

conversion.q: Fill in the blank: Energy conversion is changing energy from one ___ into another.
conversion.hint: The answer is "form". Conversion changes energy's form.

conversion.q: Which term means the process of changing energy from one form into another?
conversion.hint: The answer is "Energy conversion". That is the meaning of energy conversion.

conversion.q: A lamp converts electrical energy into which forms?
conversion.hint: The answer is "Light and heat". A lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.

conversion.q: Which is an example of energy conversion?
options: A rock sitting still on the ground
A book resting on a shelf
A toaster changing electrical energy into heat
conversion.hint: The answer is "A toaster changing electrical energy into heat". The toaster changes energy from one form into another.

conversion.q: Which is NOT an example of energy conversion?
options: A pencil lying still on a desk
A fan spinning when plugged in
conversion.hint: The answer is "A pencil lying still on a desk". Nothing is changing energy in a pencil lying still.

conversion.q: Which device converts electrical energy mainly into sound?
conversion.hint: The answer is "A doorbell". A doorbell's main job is to make sound.

conversion.q: Which device converts electrical energy mainly into motion energy?
conversion.hint: The answer is "An electric fan". A fan's blades move, so it makes motion energy.

conversion.q: Which list shows only energy conversions?
options: Rock resting, book sitting, cup standing
Fan spinning, bulb shining, radio playing
Shoe on floor, pen in cup, hat on hook
conversion.hint: The answer is "Fan spinning, bulb shining, radio playing". Each device changes electrical energy into another form.

conversion.q: You rub your hands together fast on a cold day. What energy conversion happens?
conversion.hint: The answer is "Motion energy into heat". Rubbing changes motion energy into heat, so your hands warm up.

conversion.q: Liam plugs in a radio. Electrical energy goes in. What is the main energy that comes out?
conversion.hint: The answer is "Sound". A radio converts electrical energy mainly into sound.

conversion.q: What form of energy is stored in a flashlight's batteries before you switch it on?
conversion.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy". Batteries store chemical energy.

conversion.q: Why does a light bulb feel warm after it has been on for a while?
options: Cold flows out of the bulb
Some electrical energy changes into heat
conversion.hint: The answer is "Some electrical energy changes into heat". Some energy always becomes heat when energy is converted.

conversion.q: At the science fair, Nora's solar toy car moves in the sunlight. What conversion happens?
conversion.hint: The answer is "Light energy into motion energy". The car uses the sun's light energy to move.

options: To keep energy exactly the same
To change energy from one form into another
convert.hint: The answer is "To change energy from one form into another". To convert is to change energy from one form into another.

options: Devices can convert energy into different forms
convert.hint: The answer is "Devices can convert energy into different forms". Devices change energy from one form into another.

convert.q: Fill in the blank: To ___ is to change energy from one form into another.
convert.hint: The answer is "convert". Convert means to change energy's form.

convert.q: Which word means almost the same as convert?
convert.hint: The answer is "Change". To convert energy is to change it into another form.

convert.q: When energy is converted, does any of it vanish forever?
convert.hint: The answer is "No, it just changes form". Energy never goes away; it only changes form.

convert.q: Which device converts electrical energy into heat to cook food?
convert.hint: The answer is "An electric stove". A stove changes electrical energy into heat for cooking.

convert.q: Which converts chemical energy from food into motion?
convert.hint: The answer is "Your body when you run". Your body changes food energy into motion.

options: A brick sitting in the yard
convert.hint: The answer is "A brick sitting in the yard". A brick sitting still is not changing energy.

convert.q: Which converts motion energy into sound?
options: A closed book on a shelf
A rock resting on the ground
convert.hint: The answer is "Plucking a guitar string". The moving string makes sound.

convert.q: Which converts light energy into electrical energy?
convert.hint: The answer is "A solar panel". Solar panels change light into electricity.

convert.q: A wind turbine spins in the wind. What form does it convert the motion energy into?
convert.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy". Wind turbines change motion energy into electrical energy.

convert.q: Ella stretches a rubber band and lets go, and it flies across the room. What did its stored energy convert into?
convert.hint: The answer is "Motion energy". The stretched band's stored energy changed into motion.

convert.q: You slide down a metal slide fast, and your legs feel warm. Why?
options: Heat flows from cold to hot
convert.hint: The answer is "Motion energy converts into heat". Rubbing against the slide changes some motion energy into heat.

convert.q: A battery-powered toy fan is switched on. What energy goes in and what main energy comes out?
options: Light energy in, chemical energy out
Chemical energy in, motion energy out
Sound energy in, light energy out
convert.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy in, motion energy out". The battery's chemical energy is converted into the spinning motion.

convert.q: Josh claps his hands loudly. The motion of his hands converts into which energy you can hear?
convert.hint: The answer is "Sound energy". Clapping changes motion energy into sound.
